blocks.text: Central Port Coquitlam Houses: streets and boundaries

items.t: Central Port Coquitlam is the downtown and central area around Shaughnessy Street and Wilson Avenue, between the Coquitlam River to the west and Mary Hill to the east; the City publishes no surveyed boundary for this board sub-area.
Port Coquitlam Station at 2125 Kingsway Avenue and the Port Coquitlam Community Centre at 2150 Wilson Avenue anchor the core; Shaughnessy Street is the main north–south downtown corridor.
The Official Community Plan (OCP) Bylaw, 2013, No. 3838 identifies Downtown as a mixed-use neighbourhood inside this central area, distinct from the established neighbourhoods named in the plan.

blocks.text: Central Port Coquitlam Houses: the housing stock

items.t: Detached houses here are the older central side-street stock off Shaughnessy Street, Elgin Avenue and Donald Street, sitting beside the downtown apartment zones rather than in a post-war subdivision pattern like Mary Hill.

Apartment zones RA1 and RA2 in Zoning Bylaw No. 3630 are concentrated downtown and along main roads, so a detached house on a Shaughnessy Street or Kelly Avenue lot can carry apartment zoning, not a house zone.

Detached houses are freehold; the zone and Official Community Plan designation for a central lot must be checked parcel by parcel in PoCoMAP, because house and apartment designations meet street by street downtown.

blocks.text: Central Port Coquitlam Houses: rules that affect buyers

items.t: The area around Port Coquitlam Station is one of the City's Transit-Oriented Areas in the Official Community Plan, so lots near Wilson Avenue and Kingsway Avenue sit under transit-oriented policies, not only house policies.

RA1 allows a floor area ratio of 1.0, rising where parking is underground or in a structure; RA2 allows up to 2.5, per Zoning Bylaw No. 3630 — confirm the current zone for a Shaughnessy Street lot before assuming house-only use.

blocks.text: Central Port Coquitlam Houses: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: Gates Park at 2300 Reeve Street and the Port Coquitlam Community Centre and Terry Fox Library at 2150 Wilson Avenue are both inside this central area, not across town.
The Traboulay PoCo Trail loops through the central riverfront, and ƛ̓éxətəm Regional Park (formerly Colony Farm) sits on the Coquitlam River at the area's west edge.
Port Coquitlam Station's park-and-ride is listed by TransLink at 267 spaces, open 7 days a week, 4 a.m. to 2 a.m. — useful for a house buyer who will drive to the train, not walk.
Agricultural Land Reserve land sits in and around Colony Farm at the west edge, so a lot near the Coquitlam River needs an Agricultural Land Reserve check as well as a flood check.

items.t: Central-specific point: a central house with a secondary suite is billed for both the main dwelling and the suite for water and sewer, the same suite rule stated in the Mary Hill note.

blocks.text: Central Port Coquitlam Houses: getting around

items.t: Port Coquitlam Station in this area is a West Coast Express stop between Coquitlam Central Station and Pitt Meadows Station, on the Waterfront Station to Mission City line.
Routes 173 and 174 serve the north side from Port Coquitlam Station via Wilson Avenue and Shaughnessy Street; route 170 stays on the Mary Hill side and does not serve the downtown house streets.
Lougheed Highway (Highway 7) and the Mary Hill Bypass (Highway 7B) cross the city at this area's edges, and the R3 Lougheed Hwy RapidBus runs along Lougheed Highway.

blocks.text: Central Port Coquitlam Houses: risks and due diligence

items.t: Check flood status per lot on the City flood page: Port Coquitlam has two floodplains, the Fraser/Pitt River zone and the Coquitlam River zone, and the City patrols and maintains dikes and pump stations.
Check the Watercourse Development Permit position before clearing or building near the Coquitlam River or a ditch: work in a designated watercourse area needs a permit or a City-confirmed exemption.
Check Tree Bylaw, 2019, No. 4108 before removing a mature central-lot tree: a cutting permit can be refused in bird nesting season without a biological survey.

blocks.text: Jared's take on Central Port Coquitlam
Downtown Port Coquitlam’s core is Central Port Coquitlam. For house buyers, the big question is how close they want to be to the West Coast Express station and the Shaughnessy Street shops.
Central Port Coquitlam home prices: what sold, November 2025 to October 2026

12 houses sold in Central Port Coquitlam with a median price of $1,210,000 (the middle half sold between $1,052,250 and $1,355,000), taking a median of 28 days to sell at 97.7% of the last list price; 8% sold above list. They had a median $576 per square foot, a median year built of 1974 and a median lot of 4,976 square feet.
